meta.decision_deadline_note: scaled to the armed-goal count: a judgment batch judges goals sequentially (percept/agent.py:4090), so the shipped single-goal 1.9 s budget cancels a 73-goal batch wholesale (percept/runtime/worker.py:1120)

per_goal.goal_text: Alert me when the video provides specific details about the number of casualties.
Count how many different toy vehicles are prominently featured in the play area. Only count items on the floor or table that the child or car interacts with, ignoring background toys on shelves.
Count how many legendary tribes are introduced.
Count how many times the narrator is shown on screen.

accounting.cost_caveat: Tokens are measured only on calls that RETURNED a usage row. A call the pool cancelled at the 1.5 s deadline may still have been billed by the provider; the fraction of such calls is reported so the figure can be read as a LOWER bound.

limits: Entity observations come from a harness-local motion-blob detector, not a semantic detector. Track counts are counts of MOVING REGIONS, not of people or objects. The association/eviction logic measured is the shipped EntityGraph, unmodified.

Episode numbers come from probe logs driven through the public count_event API on unregistered goal ids. They measure EpisodeLog under the shipped Settings bounds; they do NOT show the armed watches opening episodes, because watch goals never do (see the episode section).
The decision deadline is scaled to the goal count and is therefore NOT the shipped operating point. Every allocation number is a number for THAT deadline.
Cost is measured tokens x a declared price, and only calls that returned a usage row carry tokens. Cancelled calls may still have been billed: the figure is a lower bound.
One source, one provider, one model, one day, one machine.
